source_analysis: Identify physical quantities, units, derivations, conceptual assumptions, experiments and figures with source locations.
lesson_planning: Build concept intuition before formal equations; allocate time to unit interpretation, physical examples and relevant misconceptions.
slides: Keep vectors, signs, units, graph axes and scientific notation correct; use readable and complete plots or multipart figures.
narration: Define physical variables and units on first use, explain equations in natural spoken English and distinguish variable names from ordinary words.
highlighting: Anchor narration to the relevant equation line, graph region, physical vector or experiment diagram without obscuring notation.
quality_review: Flag unsupported physical claims, incorrect dimensional reasoning, ambiguous symbols or missing assumptions for review.
